Product development used to mean manually writing code, running analysis, diagnosing bugs, and rolling out changes using dozens of tools.

PostHog is the only platform that acts like a co-pilot for you (and your AI agents) to do it all – autonomously.

We started with open-source product analytics, launched out of Y Combinator's W20 cohort https://posthog.com/handbook/story. We've since shipped more than a dozen products https://posthog.com/products, including:

 1. Product-led. More than 450,000 organizations have installed PostHog, mostly driven by word-of-mouth. We have intensely strong product-market fit.

 2. Default alive https://paulgraham.com/aord.html. Revenue is growing incredibly quickly, and we're very efficient. We raise money to push ambition and grow faster, not to keep the lights on.

 3. Well-funded. We've raised more than $180m from some of the world's top investors. We're set up for a long, ambitious journey.

We're focused on building an awesome product for end users, hiring exceptional teammates, shipping fast, and being as weird as possible https://posthog.com/deskhog. 

 


THINGS WE CARE ABOUT

 - Transparency: Everyone can read about our roadmap, how we pay (or even let go of) people, our strategy, and how we work, in our public company handbook https://posthog.com/handbook. Internally, we share revenue, notes and slides from board meetings, and fundraising plans, so everyone has the context they need to make good decisions.

 - Autonomy: We don’t tell anyone what to do. Everyone chooses what to work on next based on what's going to have the biggest impact on our customers, and what they find interesting and motivating to work on. Engineers lead product teams https://posthog.com/handbook/wide-company and make product decisions https://posthog.com/handbook/which-products. Teams are flexible and easy to change when needed.

 - Shipping fast: Why not now? https://posthog.com/handbook/values#why-not-now We want to build a lot of products; we can't do that shipping at a normal pace. We've built the company around small teams – autonomous, highly-efficient groups of cracked engineers https://posthog.com/founders/cracked-manifesto who can outship much larger companies because they own their products end-to-end.

 - Time for building: Nothing gets shipped in a meeting. We're a natively remote company. We default to async communication – PRs > Issues > Slack. Tuesdays and Thursdays are meeting-free days https://posthog.com/handbook/company/culture#were-on-the-makers-schedule, and we prioritize heads down building time over perfect coordination. This will be the most productive job you've ever had.

 - Ambition: We want to solve big problems. We strongly believe that aiming for the best possible upside, and sometimes missing, is better than never trying. We're optimistic about what's possible and our ability to get there.

 - Being weird: Weird means redesigning an already world-class website for the 5th time. It means shipping literally every product that relates to customer data. It means building an objectively unnecessary developer toy https://posthog.com/deskhog with dubious shareholder value. Doing weird stuff is a competitive advantage. And it's fun.




WHO WE'RE LOOKING FOR

We’re hiring a Data Scientist for Sales and CS at PostHog to join a small team that works out which accounts are about to grow, before the growth shows up on an invoice. The holy grail is the cold start: patterns that carry over to companies who aren't using PostHog yet, where we have no usage signals at all.

This is a greenfield, quantitative role at PostHog - you’ll need engineering chops, statistical judgment, but also a keen commercial sense and an interest in working with usage time-series data. Perhaps you’re a former technical founder who did a lot of sales calls and knows how annoying it is to not have the right data at your fingertips. Or maybe a quantitative data scientist who has worked closely with sales teams, and likes to see a direct correlation between their work and making the line go up. Or a software engineer who has built data pipelines or internal tools for go-to-market teams, and wants to own the models as well as the systems that feed them. We’re happy to consider a range of profiles for this role!




WHAT YOU'LL BE DOING

 - Own and maintain the pipelines behind our daily account snapshots, and use them to find leading indicators of growth: what an account looks like 30, 60, and 90 days before it expands.

 - Engineer signals from usage, engagement, and firmographic time series, then stack them into scores that Sales, CS, and Onboarding act on.

 - Backtest everything point-in-time, so we know a signal would have worked before anyone acts on it.

 - Build systems that proactively flag expansion opportunities (free → paid, cross-sell, upsell), and get them in front of reps inside the tools they already use.

 - Train, ship, and monitor models that predict growth, so we stop finding out after the fact.

 - Measure whether acting on a signal changed the outcome, and kill the signals that don’t work.

Decide what to snapshot next, flag where the history can't be trusted, and document religiously so others can build on your work.

Example projects:

 - Growth benchmarks by cohort: what a normal trajectory looks like for an account of a given size, segment, and product mix, so the outliers stand out.

 - Signal stacking: measure each new signal's lift over the ones we already have.

 - Account-level usage and revenue forecasts, with uncertainty we can trust.

 - Smarter segmentation for cross-sell and retention plays (resurface leads and accounts when their trajectory changes).

 - A lookalike model for prospects, trained on what our best customers looked like from the outside before they signed up.

 - Holdout tests that separate "this signal predicts growth" from "acting on this signal causes growth".




WHAT YOU'LL BE DOING

 - Strong data analysis skills. You've turned messy, real-world business data into findings people acted on.

 - You have hands-on experience with time-series data and forecasting: panels across many accounts, sparse and irregular series, seasonality. You know the ways the data lies, and you can tell a good forecast from a lucky one.

 - You write production-quality Python and SQL.

 - You've taken a model or analysis out of the notebook and into something people use every day, including the pipelines and services around it.

 - Strong commercial focus - you really care about having an impact on revenue.

 - You have started a project from scratch. You might have led a project, been a founder previously, or built an impressive side project.

Nice to have

 - Prior experience with scoring or forecasting for revenue teams: lead scoring, propensity, churn, or expansion models, ideally at a product-led or usage-based company.

 - Experience with causal inference or experiment design.

 - Data engineering experience: you've built and run scheduled pipelines and warehouse models that other teams depend on.

 - Full-stack engineering experience, so you can build the tool that puts your signal in front of a salesperson.

 - You don’t have to be a Salesforce developer, but experience coding in Salesforce would definitely help.
